newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel denies opening Hebron street.
newsitem.headline: Israel denies opening Hebron street.

text.p: The Israeli army on Sunday removed cement barriers from a Hebron street closed to Arab traffic two years ago but denied the move was tied to PLO demands the road be opened to Palestinians.
Opening the street in the West Bank city's heart has been a key Palestinian demand in talks on implementing a long-delayed handover by Israel of most of Hebron.
"The Palestinians have stressed that without reopening it, we can't sign any protocol on Hebron," said Palestinian Minister of Communications Ali al-Qawasmeh.
Witnesses said Israeli bulldozers removed the cement blockades at entrances to al-Shuhada (martyrs) street but that Palestinian traffic was still barred.

"We were informed by the Israelis on Saturday night that they would work on the gradual reopening of the street, and they would start by removing the cement blocks," said a PLO official, speaking on condition of anonymity.

An Israeli army statement confirmed the cement blockades had been removed but said they were replaced with heavy plastic barriers: "It should be emphasised that all barriers remain in place and traffic regulations on Shuhada street have not changed."

The street was closed in February 1994 after a Jewish settler massacred 29 Arabs at Hebron's al-Ibrahimi mosque, also known as the Tomb of the Patriarchs. Most fortified enclaves in which the 400 Jews of Hebron live amid its 100,000 Palestinians are along al-Shuhada street.
Two months of PLO-Israeli talks on implementing the Hebron handover, agreed last year by the previous Israeli government, have not produced a deal.
